answer_text:
Let  
\[
a=BC,\qquad \angle ABC=B,\qquad \angle ACB=C.
\]
Since \(\angle BAC=60^\circ\), we have  
\[
B+C=120^\circ.
\]

Because \(\triangle ABC\) is acute, its circumcenter \(O\) lies inside the triangle, so \(D\) lies on segment \(AB\) and \(E\) lies on segment \(AC\).

Since \(O\) is the circumcenter, \(OB=OC\), and the central angle subtending chord \(BC\) is
\[
\angle BOC=2\angle BAC=120^\circ.
\]
Thus \(\triangle BOC\) is isosceles with vertex angle \(120^\circ\), so
\[
\angle OBC=\angle BCO=30^\circ.
\]

Now consider \(\triangle BCD\). Since \(D\) lies on \(CO\),
\[
\angle BCD=\angle BCO=30^\circ.
\]
Also \(D\) lies on \(AB\), so
\[
\angle CBD=\angle CBA=B.
\]
Hence
\[
\angle BDC=180^\circ-B-30^\circ=150^\circ-B.
\]
By the Law of Sines in \(\triangle BCD\),
\[
\frac{BD}{\sin 30^\circ}=\frac{BC}{\sin(150^\circ-B)},
\]
so
\[
BD=\frac{a\sin30^\circ}{\sin(150^\circ-B)}
=\frac{a}{2\sin(150^\circ-B)}.
\]

Similarly, in \(\triangle CBE\), since \(E\) lies on \(BO\),
\[
\angle CBE=\angle CBO=30^\circ,
\]
and since \(E\) lies on \(AC\),
\[
\angle BCE=\angle BCA=C.
\]
Thus
\[
\angle CEB=180^\circ-C-30^\circ=150^\circ-C.
\]
By the Law of Sines,
\[
CE=\frac{a\sin30^\circ}{\sin(150^\circ-C)}
=\frac{a}{2\sin(150^\circ-C)}.
\]

Because \(B+C=120^\circ\), we have
\[
150^\circ-C=150^\circ-(120^\circ-B)=30^\circ+B.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\sin(150^\circ-C)=\sin(30^\circ+B)=\sin(150^\circ-B).
\]
So the denominators for \(BD\) and \(CE\) are equal, giving
\[
BD=CE.
\]

Hence
\[
\frac{BD}{CE}=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
